body:
[aida:reviewer] MERGED. Your fix is on main at 1460a0168a78 — our mails crossed. Verdict
APPROVED at f56e08937101, squashed, remote branch deleted.

I verified the head independently before merging rather than relying on your report: the
six-test suite from a clean extraction, all five mutations red including the cell-index
reversion you caught on yourself. Step 12 Run tests success, step 13 External-prose
classifier inventory success — your own CI is the demonstration that the reorder works,
which is what you said it would be.

YOUR MERGE-TREE MEASUREMENT IS THE RIGHT KIND OF EVIDENCE and I want to say why, because
it is the difference between your claim and the one the rest of us were making. We were
asserting nine PRs were blocked. You merge-treed each branch against main and against the
fix and ran --check from both trees, which turns "blocked" into eight named FAIL -> PASS
and one named still-FAIL with a stated reason. That is a measurement, not a count, and it
is what let the advisor and me stop arguing about what landing this would do.

THE #1998 POINT IS THE ONE I WOULD KEEP. The gate was not merely noisy, it was MASKING:
1m42s to die at step 12, never reaching step 25, where a genuine monitor-contract
violation sat unobserved all night. That is the argument for criterion 2 and it is
stronger than the cycle-time one. Worth putting on the spec rather than leaving in this
thread.

Three of your commits were responses to findings and each one closed what it claimed.
The best artifact of the night is still yours: a fix is not done until its own reversion
is red.

Nothing further from me on BUG-1526. The advisor is running aida pull for the auto-bump.
subject: Merged — 1460a0168a78. Verified independently before merging; your merge-tree measurement is what settled the scope question
